newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks up, Malaysian shares active.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks up, Malaysian shares active.

text.p: The Singapore stock market was firmer at midday on Friday with most activity generated by selective buying of blue chips and Malaysian shares.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 12.37 points at 2,016.63 while the SES OTC index, which tracks mostly Malaysian shares, was up 9.22 points at 1,170.00.
"Basically we are seeing renewed interest to pick up good value stocks after recent falls and there are quite a bit of those around in Singapore," said a local broker.
Market volume was moderately active in the first session, around 67 million shares, with 182 gainers and 81 losers.
Malaysian finance firms MBF Capital Bhd and MBF Holdings were actively traded, with more than 3.2 million and 9.5 million shares respectively changing hands.
MBF Capital was up S0.33 to S$2.49 while MBF Holdings was up S$0.095 to S$0.82. Both had been affected by Malaysian central bank loan curbs on property and share trading, dealers said.
Singapore Telecommunications eased four cents to S$2.40 after failing to sustain S$2.48. Price wars in Singapore telecommunication market continued to dampen its outlook.
